goal: Independently review three materially different KEP hero treatments before any option is presented to the user.
context: Exact product target: cyberAlchemy-v2/product/knowledge-exchange-protocol/capabilities/hosted-devnet-exchange/v1/implementation/static/index.html and static/assets/brand.css. Current requirement: keep the orb above the CyberAlchemy Exchange title; place the KEP meaning below the title; remove the black card; preserve the tooltip, CyberAlchemy palette, centered responsive composition, white-paper and Enter Exchange actions, and protocol meaning { A } -> { A, B }. Public reference evidence: https://flywheel.paradigma.inc/ for a model-led hero and documentation/explore split; https://minaprotocol.com/ for a thesis-first protocol hero with proof notation; https://world.org/ for a single-idea hero organized around an orb-like identity asset. Candidate A, Protocol Signature: a compact single typographic line, KEP / Knowledge Expansion Protocol / { A } -> { A, B }, using restrained hierarchy and no container surface. Candidate B, Transformation Statement: make { A } -> { A, B } the primary readable line and place Knowledge Expansion Protocol as its quiet explanatory caption. Candidate C, Diagrammatic Rail: place { A } and { A, B } at opposite ends of a thin amber transition line, with KEP and its expansion integrated as a small centered legend. Each reviewer reads both exact target files and all three candidate specifications, attacks all three for hierarchy, brand fit, comprehensibility, responsiveness, and non-generic visual character, while serving as the designated primary reviewer for one candidate. Review is read-only, inline, and has no authority to edit, select, publish, deploy, or change protocol meaning.
anti_bias_global: editorial restraint versus immediate protocol comprehension versus distinctive model-led expression

groups.anti_bias: different primary design thesis with mandatory cross-option attack

predicted_disagreements.question: Should brand authority come from a compact protocol signature or from making the ownership transformation the dominant readable statement?
Does a minimal typographic signature feel more premium than a diagrammatic rail, or merely less distinctive?
Is immediate semantic clarity more important than preserving the orb-and-transition visual metaphor in the first viewport?
